# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s146) | **#888 MERGED `9e9a88709` (tree predicted and matched) · KS-968 filed MAJOR · and it LED with its own reasoning being wrong** (2026-09-07 16:13) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **THE MERGE IS TEXTBOOK:** tree oid `f83f69c01…` predicted BEFORE and identical after · **parents re-derived FROM THE OBJECT, not the API response** · containment both directions **with a control** (develop does NOT contain `74c0b3bbf`/#890, so the check discriminates) · F1 re-confirmed on develop. **AND IT LED WITH ITS OWN ERROR, which it had put in three artefacts.** It had argued the 23505 came from rewriting the address onto the row found BY that address. **Wrong — writing the same address back onto the row that holds it cannot collide with itself.** It **verified the gate's mechanism on `origin/develop` before filing rather than taking it on trust**: `if (byId)` at `:1363` rewrites the hash, the catch logs and `continue`s without rethrowing, and `if (emailRowIsDistinct)` sits at `:1388` — **after the throwing statement, so its own F3 arm never executes when both rows exist.** **Its formulation is the keeper and it is a shape this brain had not named: *"I had a real measurement and attached it to the wrong statement, which is a costlier error than not measuring at all, because it looks like evidence."*** The unique-index measurement was sound; the inference drawn from it was not. **Corrected in THREE places rather than one, *"since the wrong version was quoted onward"* — and by COMMENT, not by editing, because deleting it would leave the onward quotes unexplained.** That is the retraction-delivery rule applied without being told. **It added a finding nobody asked for: the SWALLOWING CATCH is part of the defect** — *"a remediation whose failure is indistinguishable from success at `logger.error` level is the same class as KS-962's `debug`-level seed failure. Two instances, same shape, same afternoon."* **And board hygiene most seats would have missed: it moved KS-966 back to `In Progress`** because the merge auto-transitioned it to `In Review`, *"which would have read as done-pending-sign-off while the rest of the rotation went quiet"* — items 3+4 are still open on that ticket. **KS-968 item 3 says do NOT probe the demo: likelihood UNKNOWN, and that probe is Kam's to authorise.** |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s146) | **THE DEPLOY — develop `632f16dfe` live on the Secuura demo, 31/31 images, 33 containers healthy, residue MEASURED at 3** (2026-09-07 15:50, on Kam's 13:40 word lifting Wednesday's hold) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **VERIFIED BY ARTEFACT WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL, which is what makes the verification a measurement rather than a list.** Each of the five merges confirmed by a content marker in the DEPLOYED image — and then **its own UNMERGED KS-952 work (`dist/rateLimitScope.js`) checked and found ABSENT**, so the markers discriminate between what shipped and what did not instead of everything answering PRESENT. Anchoring booted `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"` — the runbook's mandatory post-redeploy check, run rather than assumed. **KAM'S IDENTITY, the four-part statement delivered exactly as constrained: 10 files BEFORE → 3 AFTER**, all three host-side `dist/` output the rsync excludes by design, **with the control that makes it mean something — the fictional identity 0 files → 7** — and measured **INSIDE the running container** (auth: fictional 1x, real address 0x), not merely on disk. **It did not blur the half that did not happen:** the `…060` row is unchanged, and it carried the staging consequence forward — fix KS-962 a
